verdict.rationale: Snowflake documents some built-in event-to-action automation: resource monitors can be set to suspend a warehouse when it hits a credit limit, and Snowpipe loads files automatically as soon as they arrive in a stage. Streams record table changes 'so that actions can be taken,' but the evidence shows no mechanism that turns those changes into actions, so streams are only a building block. These are narrow, domain-specific triggers rather than a general rule engine. Missing for 10: a general-purpose user-defined event→action rule mechanism (e.g., tasks or alerts on arbitrary conditions), documentation of acting on stream changes, AI-native rule authoring, and independent corroboration.
